components.name: Primary Search Button
components.description: The one blue action; runs the description search.

components.name: Selected Result Tile
components.description: The selected keyframe tile; the selection must be unmistakable at a glance.
components.css: .ds-tile { position: relative; display: block; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16/9; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; border: 2px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 12px; background: #fff; cursor: pointer; } .ds-thumb { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #cbd5e1; } .ds-meta { position: absolute; left: 6px; bottom: 6px; max-width: calc(100% - 3rem); overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 4px; background: #0f172a; color: #fff; font: 500 10px ui-monospace, monospace; } .ds-tile-selected { border-color: #2563eb; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #f7f7f5, 0 0 0 4px rgba(37,99,235,.5); } .ds-tile-selected .ds-thumb { background: #93c5fd; } .ds-tile-selected .ds-meta { background: #2563eb; font-weight: 600; } .ds-check { position: absolute; right: 6px; bottom: 6px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: #2563eb; color: #fff; }

components.description: Every keyframe of the selected video; arrow keys step, wheel scrolls horizontally.

narrative.overview: The operator is working against a clock, so the interface behaves like a clean cutting bench: the frame is the object, the chrome is thin and quiet, and the next action is always one key away. The screen is near-white and charcoal, with exactly two accents doing real jobs: blue for action and selection, green for commit and correct. Everything else is a hairline. This is deliberately the standard search console, chosen by the operator over a distinctive visual world. Its character comes from precision, scale, and restraint rather than ornament. The keyframe is always unobstructed; no hover preview, gradient scrim, or overlay chip covers the image.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white canvas, charcoal ink, 1px hairlines, 12px media corners.
One large stage and a 2-up keyframe wall; the images are the only saturated color.
Keyboard spine: /, Enter, arrows, Space, [ ], S, C, R, T, F, ?.
A pinned submit bar with an inline video ID and timestamp, plus video-ID lookup.
Flat surfaces; only popovers and dialogs lift.

rules.name: The Two Accents Rule
rules.body: Blue means action or selection; green means commit or correct. Neither is decorative, and green never becomes a status dot.

rules.name: The Frame Carries Color Rule
rules.body: Keyframe images are the only saturated field on a working screen. Chrome stays neutral so the frame wins.

rules.name: The Unobstructed Frame Rule
rules.body: No hover preview, gradient scrim, or overlay chip covers a frame. Metadata belongs in the toolbar or below the media.

rules.name: The Data Is Monospaced Rule
rules.body: IDs, timestamps, scores, and keycaps use the mono stack with tabular numerals; prose never does.

rules.name: The Flat Until It Floats Rule
rules.body: Cards and regions are flat at rest; only popovers and dialogs carry a shadow.

dos: Do keep the frame unobstructed; put metadata in the toolbar or below the media.
Do use blue for action/selection and green only for commit/correct.
Do make the selected tile unmistakable with a border, ring, blue chips, and a check.
Do keep the keyboard spine and the video-ID Enter lookup.
Do keep the full-video strip below the follow frames, with arrow stepping and wheel scrolling.
Do use mono and tabular numerals for IDs, timestamps, scores, and keys.
donts: Don't add hover-to-zoom or floating previews over images.
Don't overlay gradient scrims or chips on frames.
Don't reintroduce a filter sidebar or a visual-world costume.
Don't show retrieval scores in video-lookup mode.
Don't use green or blue decoratively.
Don't signal selection with a 1px border alone.
